one_line: Add one named constant, WIRE_NAME, whose value is deliberately still the string "omp", and point the five third-party contract sites at it so the next rename has one place to change instead of five — and, because four of the five already have golden-literal tests, so that renaming it breaks a test instead of a user's Warp terminal or ACP client.

effort: S for the source change (six files, one added line in dirs.ts and five one-to-three-line edits), S for the test (one new ~15-line file, zero edits to existing tests). Net roughly 40 lines of diff across 7 paths. The plan's "~10 lines" understates it by not counting the new test file, but the plan's instinct that this is the cheapest item in the wave is right. The one thing that could blow it up is the DAP test — gate (6) exists specifically to stop that from happening.
risk: Typing the new brand name into WIRE_NAME.
gate:
The change is DONE when all of the following hold, and the first one is the one that can fail:

(1) `bun test packages/utils/test/wire-name.test.ts` FAILS if `WIRE_NAME` is not exactly the string "omp" — verified by temporarily setting it to "ultraworkers" and confirming a red run, then reverting. This is the load-bearing gate: it is the only thing that pins the constant itself, and it is the whole defence against the failure mode the plan calls out first.
(2) `bun run check:ts` is green.
(3) All four existing golden test files are byte-identical to HEAD — `git diff packages/coding-agent/test/ packages/catalog/` is EMPTY. If any of them changed, the engineer converted a golden pin into a tautology and the item is not done, regardless of whether tests pass.
(4) `git diff --stat` lists exactly the six modified source files plus the one new test file, and `packages/catalog/src/wire/codex.ts` is not among them.
(5) `git grep -n '"omp"'` over the four coding-agent source files that had bare literals returns zero hits, while `acp-agent.ts` retains `name: "oh-my-pi"` on line 656.
(6) `packages/coding-agent/src/dap/session.ts` shows no new test file and no new export — the DAP gap was closed transitively, as documented, rather than by adding a harness.
gate_can_fail: Yes, and gate (1) is the one that bites. It goes red the moment someone writes `export const WIRE_NAME: string = "ultraworkers";` — which is the single most likely mistake here, because the whole point of the constant is to be renamed and the new brand name is the most attractive thing in the repo to type. The four existing goldens are a second, independent net for the same mistake (they compare against literal "omp"), and gate (3) catches the subtler failure where an engineer "helpfully" rewrites those goldens to compare against the constant, which would make all five sites pass a rename silently. Gate (4) catches scope creep — the plan itself warns that adding a sixth site is the second-most-likely error, and `git grep` over the whole repo finds several more bare "omp" wire values (see plan_corrections) that an eager engineer would fold in without deciding. Nothing in this gate is a tautology or a bare not.toThrow(); every clause names a value a third party reads.

title: Split config-directory resolution into a dual-root read side and a single-root write side, and add ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR as an alias that beats PI_CONFIG_DIR
one_line: Make ~/.omp and ~/.ultraworkers both readable by resolving the config root as an ordered candidate list, while every new write and the install-id's write path go only to the new root, and make the project-level .omp directory and the two Rust env readers exempt.
user_visible_effect: A user who upgrades mid-flight never loses their settings, sessions or install identity: an install that only has the old root keeps reading it, an install that has both prefers the new one, an install with neither falls back to the default, and everything newly written lands in the new root.
depends_on: W3 (must land first so the new APP_NAME value exists; W4 writes that name, and without W3 there is no name to write — the plan is explicit that W4 depends on W3 for this reason)
M2 (merged, so the legacy-pi-compat table is frozen; M5 and M2 both touch it)
blocks: W5 (config migrate moves ~/.omp to ~/.ultraworkers and $XDG_*/omp to $XDG_*/ultraworkers; it needs the dual-root read to know both roots exist and needs the separated write root to place files)
W6 (flipping CONFIG_DIR_NAME is meaningless without a read side that still finds the legacy root — the whole point of the hard gate is that W6 changes only where NEW writes land)
W6a (the project-root pin lands here, early, because W4 is what makes the home-side name diverge)
effort: M. The candidate list itself is small — roughly 40 lines across one module. What makes it M rather than S is that three separate mechanisms each have their own way of failing quietly: splitting install-id read from write while keeping UUID validation and the O_EXCL create race intact; adding a cache to an accessor that the module already freezes in four different places; and keeping the project-level and Rust paths off the home-side name. The plan calls this M and that rating holds.
risk: The dominant risk is a failure that produces no error, no warning, and no failing test at the moment it ships.
gate:
Run from the repo root.

  bun run check:ts
  cd packages/utils && bun test ./test/config-dir-dual-root.test.ts ./test/install-id-legacy-read.test.ts ./test/config-dir-write-root.test.ts
  cd ../.. && bun test ./packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts ./packages/utils/test/profiles.test.ts ./packages/utils/test/dirs-python-gateway.test.ts ./packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts

The leading './' on each path is required: without it Bun treats the argument as a name filter rather than a path, and the missing-file case still exits 1 but the real-file case reports '0 tests' in a way that is easy to misread as green.

RED-BEFORE-GREEN is mandatory for contract (2). Before the getInstallId() change, planting a UUID at the legacy install-id path and resolving with the new root empty returns a DIFFERENT freshly minted UUID, and the assertion that the planted value comes back fails. That is a true red, not a missing-file error, and it is the only proof that the change is doing anything.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, so a vacuous green is impossible: before trusting the suite, confirm each new file reports a non-zero pass count. A file that loads and reports '0 pass' has asserted nothing. The missing-file control above (exit 1) plus a deliberate temporary break in getConfigWriteRootName() (return the legacy name, expect contract 3 and contract 4 to go red) together establish that these tests can actually fail.

REGRESSION NET: packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts must pass UNCHANGED — it pins the current single-root install-id behaviour, so it is what proves the resolver rewiring did not disturb an unrelated contract.

CROSS-PACKAGE, NO NEW AUTOMATED GATE: `bun test ./packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts` covers the helpers.ts rewiring on the TypeScript side. The two Rust files have no test harness in this milestone — `bun run check:rs` type-checks them, and the darwin.rs path in particular is macOS-only, so a reviewer must read those two hunks rather than rely on a run. Say so in the PR rather than implying a green run covered them.
gate_can_fail:
Yes, in five ways that were each verified against the real tree rather than assumed.

(a) Mint instead of read. If getInstallId() falls through to generating a new UUID when only the legacy path is readable, contract (2) goes red. Verified that this is a TRUE red rather than an environment problem: the probe above shows the read accessor is live, so a planted legacy file really is found by the test. This is the single failure that silently costs money — a new UUID is indistinguishable from a correct one at every call site, and the only symptom is a cost table restarting.

(b) Do not clear the cache. If refreshDirsFromEnv() (:484), setAgentDir() (:502) and setProfile() (:541) do not call the new reset, the eight test files that assign process.env.PI_CONFIG_DIR at runtime read a frozen root and go red. Verified list in step 6. This is the failure mode that would make the change look correct in a fresh single-test run and break the wider suite — precisely why the third gate command includes packages/utils/test/profiles.test.ts and packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts.

(c) Leave the project path on the home accessor. If helpers.ts:1032/:1034/:1049/:1079 still call getConfigDirName(), every project with a committed .omp stops resolving its installed_plugins.json the moment the new root wins. Note the failure is deferred: at W4 the new root is never created, so this passes today and breaks at W5/W6. The negative control in the gate (deliberately flipping getConfigWriteRootName to the legacy name) is what surfaces it inside W4 rather than three items later.

(d) Share one candidate list between the home and XDG spellings. The home root is dot-prefixed, the XDG appRoot is not (dirs.ts:360 joins APP_NAME). One shared list is wrong for exactly one of the two, and the wrong one is invisible on a machine without XDG_*_HOME set — which is most CI.

(e) Extend the alias to TypeScript only. The crash-log directory (crash_handler.rs:269) and the macOS OAuth recovery path (darwin.rs:441) would keep honouring PI_CONFIG_DIR alone, so a user who sets only ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR gets a coherent config root and an incoherent crash-log directory. No test in the repo catches this; only reading the two hunks does.

Separately: the brief's claim that `bun test` is blocked on this machine is FALSE and must not be propagated. It reports 5 pass / 0 fail for install-id.test.ts and 2 pass / 0 fail for dirs-python-gateway.test.ts; the 17 failures in the full packages/utils run are the pi_natives addon and are confined to logger-contract.test.ts and procmgr.test.ts. `bun run check:ts` exits 0. The real limitation is that `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build` fails without ninja, which only matters if a change here needs the native addon rebuilt — and none of the four files W4 touches do.

title: Ship `config migrate` — idempotent, dry-run by default
one_line: Add a `migrate` subcommand to the existing `config` command that moves the user config roots from the old name to the new one (`~/.omp` → `~/.ultraworkers` and `$XDG_{DATA,STATE,CACHE}_HOME/omp` → `$XDG_*_HOME/ultraworkers`), preserving `install-id`, dry-run by default with an explicit `--apply`, and safe to run twice (second run reports 0 moves and exits 0).
user_visible_effect: `omp config migrate` prints the exact list of directories it would move and exits without touching anything.
depends_on: W4 — HARD GATE. The ordered read-candidate list (`getConfigDirCandidates`) and the separate write root (`getConfigWriteRoot`). Verified absent on HEAD: `git grep -n 'getConfigWriteRoot\|getConfigDirCandidates' -- packages/utils/src/dirs.ts` returns nothing. Without W4, `~/.omp` stops resolving the moment W6 flips, and this command is the only path back.
W3 — supplies the new name (the new `APP_NAME` value) that `MigrationOptions.newName` is set from. The XDG candidate join mirrors dirs.ts:360, which is already APP_NAME-driven.
M2 frozen (the milestone-wide baseline), per the plan's own dependency note.
blocks: W6 — HARD GATE, the stated purpose. W6 flips `CONFIG_DIR_NAME` at dirs.ts:27; the plan requires W5 to have shipped AND been used in a real release first, and W6 itself must not land before that. W5 is the user's manual path back from a bad flip.
M5 definition-of-done: a rename whose on-disk state can survive the flip is not shippable without a tested, idempotent, dry-run-by-default migration command.
effort: M, as the plan says, but the distribution is different from what it implies. The plan reads as "two files, four edit sites"; the real shape is three new files, four modified, twelve edit sites, and a reusable-move promotion in a fifth. The move logic itself is genuinely easy (a rename with an EXDEV fallback). The two things that are not easy, exactly as the plan says, are the conflict/idempotency rule and the named-profile case. Budget for the `movePath` promotion into `gc-cli.ts` — it is a cross-file refactor of a file this work item does not otherwise touch, and it is the single most likely source of an unrelated regression in this commit.
risk: Ranked by how badly it fails.
gate:
Two commands, both of which were measured on this machine before being proposed.

(1) `bun run check:ts` — exit 0 on a clean tree, verified twice, roughly 40s wall. This is the only automated signal for the eight `config-cli.ts` and four `config.ts` edit sites, and it is a weak one: a forgotten site produces no type error at all, because widening `ConfigAction` leaves `VALID_ACTIONS` and `ACTIONS` typechecking as subsets, and a `switch` over a union has no exhaustiveness check here (no `noImplicitReturns` in the tsconfig, no exhaustiveness rule in `.oxlintrc.json`). The count is a REVIEW obligation, not a tool obligation. Say so in the PR description rather than implying the typecheck caught it.

(2) `bun test packages/utils/test/config-migrate.test.ts` — this is the real gate, and it was chosen specifically because it is the only surface on this machine where the four properties under test can actually be falsified. It is red before the work starts and green only when the work is correct:
  - today, with no such file, the command exits **1** (verified: `bun test <missing-path>` → `EXIT=1`, "Tests need \".test\"… in the filename");
  - `bun test packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts` in the SAME package exits **0** with 5 pass / 0 fail (verified), because it imports the `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/dirs` subpath, which has no `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` in its graph.
  So a green here means the test ran and passed. It cannot mean "could not run".

What is explicitly NOT the gate: `cd packages/coding-agent && bun test test/config-migrate.test.ts`, the command the plan gives. On this machine it exits **1** (verified: 0 pass / 1 fail / 1 error, `Cannot find module .../packages/natives/native/pi_natives.darwin-arm64.node`) whether or not the feature is implemented, because every `packages/coding-agent` test transitively loads `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives`. Gating on it would mean a permanently red gate whose redness carries no information about the work — the failure mode the brief warns about. The plan's gate has to be rewritten, not merely run.
gate_can_fail:
Yes, and specifically in the direction that matters — it can distinguish "the engineer did the work" from "the test could not run".

The primary test gate is falsifiable in five distinct ways, each verified against the real tree rather than assumed:
(a) Implement nothing, create nothing. `bun test packages/utils/test/config-migrate.test.ts` exits 1 because the file does not exist. RED.
(b) Write the test but leave the engine's decision rule at two states (merge when both roots exist). Case 4 goes red on the marker-file assertion. RED.
(c) Write the test but make `planConfigMigration` write as it reads. Case 1 goes red on the still-exists assertions. RED.
(d) Make the executor run twice unconditionally. Case 3 goes red on the `moves.length === 0` assertion and on the byte-identical check. RED.
(e) Regenerate `install-id` during the move. Case 5 goes red on the value-equality assertion. RED.

And the negative control — the property that makes the gate trustworthy — was also verified: `bun test packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts` exits 0 in that same package on this same machine, with no work done at all. So a green in `packages/utils` is evidence of a real pass, not of a skipped suite.

The coding-agent CLI gate CANNOT fail meaningfully here, and this is stated rather than hidden: it exits 1 on a clean tree because the native addon is missing. It becomes meaningful only after `brew install ninja && bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`, and even then it is the secondary signal. Do not let it be quoted as acceptance in a PR on this machine.

blocks: W6 — this is a mandatory sub-task of W6, not an optional companion. W6 must not be merged without it; the spec is written to land first or in the same commit.
W7 — the do_not_rename row created in step 8 is part of the exclusion list W7's 4107-file sed loads
M5 definition-of-done — the 'on-disk identity shipped' condition is not true until the project root is provably still read

title: Rename the binary name the two Python packages actually spawn — the only brand occurrence Python executes — and change nothing else they mention
one_line: In `python/omp-rpc` and `python/robomp` exactly two source lines mint the binary name (`client.py:455` and `config.py:95`), plus two shipped-config overrides the plan's grep cannot see (`docker-compose.yml:81` and `.env.example:185`) that would silently defeat both edits; every other `omp` in `python/**` is a Unix group that is materialized on real hosts, a container-sandbox on-disk layout, or the CLI's own config dir owned by W4/W6, and all of them stay. The Python packages ship in the same release as W9 because between a TS-only rename and a Python rename there is a window in which the new binary has no `omp` command and the Python clients still call one.
user_visible_effect: The typed RPC client and the robomp triage bot spawn the renamed binary by default instead of failing with FileNotFoundError on `omp`.
depends_on: W9 (the binary name W9 installs is the value these four sites must carry — W13p cannot name the new command without W9, and shipping W9 without W13p leaves the Python clients calling a command that no longer exists)
blocks: W10 (its Docker work builds the image whose `/usr/local/bin/omp` shim at Dockerfile:180 and ENTRYPOINT at :216 is what `ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND` names; if W10 renames the shim and this item has not updated docker-compose.yml:81, the robomp image is built pointing at a command it no longer contains)
effort: S, not the plan's M — and the plan overcounts for a defensible reason while undercounting the inventory. The edits themselves are 6 string values across 4 code files plus 4 descriptive strings across 2 manifests: about 10 added and 10 removed lines in 7 files, with roughly 150 real `omp` occurrences left deliberately untouched. What the plan priced as M is the deliberation of enumerating 24 occurrences into three sets, and that enumeration is already done and verified here (4 / 8 / 12, per-file counts pinned), so the expensive half of the plan's estimate is spent. What it missed — the compose override, the `.omp*` family being 108 rather than 12, the `~/.omp` config-dir category, and the `robomp:22` dependency coupling — is discovery cost that this spec has already paid. Realistically half a day: 2-3 hours of edits, 1 hour reconciling the keep-list with W7's `scripts/rename/keep-list.txt`, 1 hour of gates, and the rest waiting on the two open questions below. The one thing that can stretch it is container verification, which cannot be done from this repository at all.
risk: Highest consequence, and the one the plan names correctly: editing only `client.py:455` and `config.py:95` and calling it done.
gate:
Three gates, all executed from the repo root, all verified to produce the stated result on HEAD 84cbac9 BEFORE any edit. Gates 1 and 2 are tripwires (red now, green after the work); gate 3 is an invariant (green now, green after, RED on a partial rename) and is the one that catches the failure this item is actually about.

--- GATE 1 — THE SPLIT (tripwire: RED today) ---
CHANGED=$(git grep -c '"omp"' -- python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py python/robomp/src/config.py python/omp-rpc/tests/test_client.py 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
KEPT=$(git grep -c '"omp"' -- python/omp-rpc/tests/test_user_group.py python/robomp/src/worker.py python/robomp/src/sandbox.py python/robomp/tests/test_sandbox.py python/robomp/tests/test_worker.py 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' | cut -d: -f2 | paste -sd, -)
echo "set_i_files_still_matching=$CHANGED keep_counts=$KEPT"
[ "$CHANGED" = "0" ] && [ "$KEPT" = "5,2,2,8,3" ]

Verified output today: `set_i_files_still_matching=3 keep_counts=5,2,2,8,3` → RED, as designed. The residual total is 20, not 24, and the keep counts are pinned PER FILE so that renaming a Unix group or a sandbox path cannot be masked by deleting a different keep site. `git grep -c` prints nothing for a zero-count file, which is why the changed-file check counts LINES OF OUTPUT (3 today) rather than summing hits.

--- GATE 2 — NO SHIPPED FILE PINS THE OLD NAME (tripwire: RED today) ---
OV=$(git grep -ohE 'ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND[=:][[:space:]]*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*' -- python/robomp/docker-compose.yml python/robomp/.env.example | awk -F'[=:] *' '{print $2}' | paste -sd, -)
echo "shipped_overrides=[$OV]"; [ "$OV" = "ultraworkers,ultraworkers" ]

Verified output today: `shipped_overrides=[omp,omp]` → RED, as designed. This is the gate that does not exist in the plan. It targets the two files the `"omp"` grep cannot see, because there the value is unquoted-at-line-start and preceded by the variable name.

--- GATE 3 — FOUR-WAY NAME AGREEMENT (invariant: GREEN today, RED on a partial rename) ---
C=$(grep -oE 'executable: str = "[^"]+"' python/omp-rpc/src/omp_rpc/client.py | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"')
R=$(grep -oE 'omp_command: str = Field\("[^"]+"' python/robomp/src/config.py | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"')
D=$(grep -oE 'ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND: *[^ ]+' python/robomp/docker-compose.yml | awk '{print $2}')
E=$(grep -oE 'ROBOMP_OMP_COMMAND=[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*' python/robomp/.env.example | cut -d= -f2)
echo "client=$C config=$R compose=$D env=$E"
{ [ -n "$C" ] && [ "$C" = "$R" ] && [ "$C" = "$D" ] && [ "$C" = "$E" ]; }

Verified output today: `client=omp config=omp compose=omp env=omp` → GREEN (all four agree today). This gate is the structural mirror of §3.1: a consumer reads a name from a constant while a producer hardcodes the literal elsewhere, and nothing executes either. It stays green through a correct rename and goes red the moment one of the four is missed — most valuably if `config.py` is changed and `docker-compose.yml` is not, which is precisely the mistake gate 1 alone would report as success.

--- ENVIRONMENT-SUFFIXED GATE — the behavioural one, WITH a runnable-prefix check ---
Run ONLY if the prefix prints READY. On this machine the prefix FAILS (`python3 -m pytest --version` → `No module named pytest`), and the gate must then report NOT-RUNNABLE and exit non-zero — never silently pass.

  if python3 -m pytest --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo READY; else
    echo "NOT-RUNNABLE: pytest missing. Build it with:"; \
    echo "  uv venv /tmp/ompw13-venv -p 3.13"; \
    echo "  VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/ompw13-venv uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio respx httpx pydantic pydantic-settings fastapi uvicorn click python-dotenv -e python/omp-rpc -e python/robomp"; \
    exit 2; fi
  /tmp/ompw13-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q python/omp-rpc/tests   # 81 passed, 17 subtests
  /tmp/ompw13-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q python/robomp/tests      # 665 passed, 4 skipped

The two invocations must stay SEPARATE. Combined they fail at collection with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests.test_user_group'` — both directories are named `tests` and neither has `__init__.py`.
gate_can_fail:
Yes, and the reason each of the three can fail is different.

GATE 1 fails the moment a set-(i) site is missed, and — because the keep counts are per file rather than a single total — it also fails if the engineer satisfies '20 remain' by renaming a Unix group or a sandbox path. That second failure mode is the one the plan's total-count check would miss entirely: dropping `test_user_group.py` from 5 to 0 and `test_sandbox.py` from 8 to 3 both land on exactly 20. Verified red today (`set_i_files_still_matching=3`).

GATE 2 fails if `docker-compose.yml` or `.env.example` still names the old command. This is the gate for a mistake the plan does not contain, and the mistake it catches is silent: the container starts, robomp boots, and the first RPC spawn is the only evidence. Verified red today (`shipped_overrides=[omp,omp]`).

GATE 3 fails on a PARTIAL rename — any one of the four sources changed without the other three. It is the only gate here that stays green before and after and therefore functions as a regression net rather than a progress indicator. Verified green today (`client=omp config=omp compose=omp env=omp`); it must be green again only when all four read the new name.

Stated plainly so they are not over-trusted: the environment-gated pytest run cannot fail on a rename at all if the prefix is skipped — which is why the prefix exits 2 with NOT-RUNNABLE rather than falling through. `bun run check:ts` is in the plan's command line and is STRUCTURALLY BLIND here: it filters `./packages/*` and oxlint is JS/TS only, so no edit to any file in this item can turn it red. It must not be reported as evidence for this work. Nothing in this repository executes `docker-compose.yml`, so gate 3 is a static string comparison and not a behavioural proof that a container spawns the right command — a real container smoke run is the only thing that would be, and it is out of scope.
